title: The 2026 Rookie Draft: A Roast
intro: Forty-eight picks, five trades, one compensatory selection that Sleeper still refuses to acknowledge, and at least three decisions that will be screenshotted in the group chat by Halloween. The Oracle watched all of it, cross-referenced nine years of your collective nonsense, and has thoughts. Nobody asked for grades. You're getting them anyway.

1.blurb: After going 1-27 — a record so bad the double-win format awarded him losses twice a week just to be thorough — Tim finally gets a reward: the consensus best player in the class. Take a bow, Tim. It's the first thing you've won since the 2025 preseason.
The C-Men went 6-22 and drafted a smooth route-runner with alpha upside. Solid pick. Now do something about the fact that your team name still gets flagged by every spam filter in Ohio.
First of SEVEN Ben picks tonight. When you go 8-20, you don't rebuild — you file for bankruptcy and start a new identity. Price is a hell of a first brick.
Lee went 9-19 and sprinted to the podium for a QB like a man whose superflex spot was being manned by vibes and a prayer. Honestly? Correct urgency.

The commissioner, whose team is literally named after Ashton Jeanty, watched Jeanty-adjacent RBs fly off the board and took... a wide receiver. The bit is dead, Aaron. The bit died at 1.01 and you drafted its eulogy.

The reigning Toilet Bowl champion spends his first-round pick on a QB, which is what you do when your prize for winning the losers bracket is 'more draft picks' and your prize for the season was 'nothing.'

Tim's second first-rounder — acquired from Bryan, who is watching his former pick become the NFL's 8th overall selection. The catch: Tyson's already nursing a hamstring, which for a Crab Boilers player counts as arriving in mint condition.
Back-to-back first-rounders for the Maniacs, who scored the fewest points of any team not named Crab Boilers last year. When life gives you a 9-19 season, draft Lemon. Sorry. Someone had to.

David went 23-5 — the best record in league history — and lost the title anyway. Now he's drafting Niners receivers to numb the pain. This is the same franchise that once left Tom Brady and 99 points on the bench in a playoff week, so grief is kind of the brand.

The Meats hung 1,756 points last year — most in the league — and still don't own a trophy. Adding a Jets receiver to fix that is certainly *a* plan. Bold to entrust your championship window to whatever the hell is happening in East Rutherford.

The pick with more frequent-flyer miles than anyone in the league: Bortz's, then Bryan's, now Ben's — who spent it on a tight end. Somewhere Bryan is holding James Cook and feeling absolutely nothing, which is the point of the trade.

The defending champ — who's been quietly collecting titles since 2018 like it's a hobby — takes a shiny new TE with the last regular pick of round one. Rich people buying more nice things. Disgusting. Continue.

1c.blurb: The Toilet Bowl comp pick, used on a real running back — a genuinely nice outcome that is currently rostered NOWHERE, because the pick doesn't exist in Sleeper and nobody's entered him yet. Alex won the Toilet Bowl and drafted a ghost. If the commissioner doesn't process this before someone 'finds' Coleman on waivers, the ensuing shitstorm gets its own constitutional amendment. You've been warned.

2.blurb: A Chiefs running back for the man who wins everything except the thing that matters. Emmett will get you 19 wins and a Week 16 heartbreak. It's tradition now.

A bruising Raiders back so under-the-radar he wasn't even in the Oracle's database until this week. Kristian drafting players the computers haven't heard of is either genius or a cry for help. At 6-22, could be both.
Ben's third pick and we're barely into round two. At this pace the Dirty Birds' taxi squad will need its own zip code and a small municipal government.
Third pick in four selections for Lee, who is rebuilding with the focus of a man who just remembered the ACT exam exists and last place is legally binding.
A Chiefs deep threat for the commissioner. Kansas City receivers are like league constitutions: everyone's excited at the signing, then one guy gets all the targets.

A big-bodied Browns receiver named Denzel Boston, which sounds less like a football player and more like a character Denzel Washington plays in a movie about Boston. Alex is collecting names. The roster is a screenplay.
Tim's third pick of the night lands a Commanders wideout. Genuinely a nice haul forming here — which, after 1-27, is the least the football gods owe him. They owe him this and a formal apology.

The Cooper brothers grab a 6'4" Giants receiver with the pick that changed hands twice on draft day alone. Risky Business trafficking in laundered assets. The name isn't a team, it's a business model.

Back-to-back for the Coopers, and Singleton at 2.09 is the kind of value that makes the rest of the league pretend they weren't interested. You were all interested. The Oracle saw the trade block likes.
A Ravens red-zone target for the league's highest-scoring bridesmaid. The Meats stacking touchdown-dependent receivers is very on-brand for a team whose entire identity is 'almost.'

Steven — whose team name is still just his username, eight years in, a level of commitment to the bit that's honestly admirable — takes a bowling ball of a Washington back. No notes on the pick. Several notes on the branding.

Pick number FOUR for Ben. The Dirty Birds are now legally a youth academy. Branch is electric with the ball; whether anyone in this haul hits is a 2028 problem, and Ben has decided 2028 is when he starts caring.

3.blurb: A fourth Crab Boilers pick. Tim is speed-running the only rebuild in history that started from 1-27, which isn't a rebuild so much as an archaeological dig.
A Vikings back with juice. Lee's now made four picks, all of them defensible, which for a 9-19 team is the most alarming development of the entire draft. Stay bad, Lee. The ecosystem depends on it.
Ben's fifth pick is a Cardinals QB flier, because when you're assembling an ark you need two of every position. It's superflex. It's fine. It's also pick FIVE, Ben.
Ted Hurst sounds like your dad's accountant and plays receiver for Tampa Bay. The Coopers drafting a man named Ted in round three is the most confident move of the night.
A Ravens receiver with sneaky size for team swillke. Steven quietly assembling actual talent while everyone jokes about his team name is exactly how you finish 13-15 and scare nobody until Week 14.
A Bills slot man joins Denzel Boston in Alex's Cinematic Universe. The Toilet Bowl champ is drafting a cast, and honestly the chemistry read is going well.

SIX. Six picks. Ben is drafting like the league fines you for exiting with cap space. Brazzell's a lanky Carolina flier, and at this point Ben's strategy is just 'own every rookie and let God sort it out.'
The Steelers QB of the possibly-near future for the 23-5 runner-up. David hoarding quarterbacks after watching his season die is a man buying smoke detectors the week after the fire.
A Patriots tight end, which historically is where fantasy points go to enter witness protection. Lee's fifth pick of a genuinely industrious night.
The commissioner grabs a Dolphins wideout while simultaneously being the man responsible for entering Jonah Coleman into Sleeper. One of these tasks is done, Aaron.
A second QB in four picks for David — a 6'6" Browns project with legs for days. In this league's superflex economy, hoarding QBs is just fiscal responsibility with extra steps.

The champ takes a Ravens back built like a vending machine. Lyndsey drafting depth pieces while everyone else panic-rebuilds is the fantasy equivalent of showing up to a knife fight already holding the belt.

4.blurb: The commissioner opens round four with a Jets QB, officially making this a three-QB draft for teams named after running backs they don't roster.
Kristian drafts Athan Kaliakmanis, instantly leading the league in scrabble points and ensuring nobody at the 2027 draft pronounces an on-the-clock trade correctly ever again.

Ben's SEVENTH and final pick. The Dirty Birds drafted more players tonight than they won games last year, which is either poetry or a lawsuit against himself. Delp's a legit TE — the haul, top to bottom, is genuinely good. Now win a damn game.
Lee's sixth pick shares a surname with the most famous draft bust of the decade, which takes guts. A Saints receiver behind a crowded room — the definition of a fourth-round dart.

Steven quietly walks away with Jonathan Taylor's direct handcuff — a back Taylor himself compared to David Montgomery — at 4.05. The best value of the round went to the team with no name. Nobody clapped. Somebody should have.
An Eagles QB stash whose name sounds like a Madden create-a-player. Between Payton, Boston, and the ghost of Jonah Coleman, the Silver Bullets' draft class is 40% fictional characters.

Bryan traded away his entire draft — the 1.11, the 3.07, a 2027 first — for James Cook and Rico Dowdle, attended this event for one single pick, and used it on the D-II camp legend currently terrorizing the Falcons' depth chart. One pick. All gas. If Strand ever starts an NFL game, this is the smuggest man in Ohio. If not, he already got Cook, so he's the smuggest man in Ohio anyway. Shameless. Ruthless. Probably correct.
A Broncos TE with real athleticism sliding to 4.08. The Coopers' fourth pick of a sneaky-deep haul. The brothers are running a chop shop and the league keeps donating vehicles.
Five picks for Risky Business, closing with a Raiders speed merchant. Quantity AND quality, which is frankly rude to the teams that managed neither.

A Chargers burner to close the Meats' draft. 21-7 last year, most points in the league, zero rings since forever — and now more speed. The window is open. The window has BEEN open. Jacob, climb through the goddamn window.
Lee's SEVENTH pick — tying Ben for volume — on a Steelers back whose name the autocorrect will be fighting all season. The Maniacs drafted half a roster tonight. Rebuild officially has a pulse.

Mr. Irrelevant honors go to a Jaguars tight end, drafted by the reigning champ, who exits the night having done approximately nothing and remains the favorite anyway. The rich stay rich, the Toilet Bowl awaits the rest of you, and the Oracle will see everyone in Week 1.

awards.why: Seven picks, real talent at every turn, and the honesty to admit 8-20 requires demolition, not paint.
Jonathan Taylor's handcuff, praised by Taylor himself, in the fourth round. Larceny with a bib on.
One pick all night and he spent it on an undrafted D-II folk hero. Either a legend or a cautionary tale — no in-between, which is the point.
Drafted with a pick that isn't in Sleeper, currently rostered by no one. A fully constitutional ghost. Aaron, please.
NFL 8th overall pick, already questionable for Week 1. Welcome to the Crab Boilers, where health goes to die.
Three depth picks, zero sweat, still the champ. Menacingly boring.
